title: Do humans really have an aura and emit light? New study might shock you
summary:
真的存在类似光环的现象吗——人类在活着的时候是否会散发出一种微弱的光芒？如今，由加拿大卡尔加里大学与加拿大国家研究委员会的研究人员共同进行的一项实验带来了震撼性的发现：这种微光或许真的存在。该研究还发现，当生命走向终点时，这道微弱的光芒也会随之消失。相关成果已发表在《物理化学快报》上。

来源：Pennlive.com；作者：EmilyAnn Jackman；原文发布时间：2025-05-18 21:40:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Is there really such thing as an aura — a light that humans give off while they are alive? A shocking discovery in an experiment conducted by researchers from the University of Calgary and the National Research Council of Canada suggests we do. And, when we die, the study suggests that faint light goes away. The research was published in The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters.
paragraphs.contentZh: 真的存在类似光环的现象吗——人类在活着的时候是否会散发出一种微弱的光芒？如今，由加拿大卡尔加里大学与加拿大国家研究委员会的研究人员共同进行的一项实验带来了震撼性的发现：这种微光或许真的存在。该研究还发现，当生命走向终点时，这道微弱的光芒也会随之消失。相关成果已发表在《物理化学快报》上。

paragraphs.contentEn: The extraordinary experiment began with mice and leaves from two different plant species and it uncovered spot-on physical evidence of a bizarre “biophoton” anomaly that stops upon death. So, this suggests that all living things – including humans – could quite literally glow while alive.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这项不同寻常的实验起初以小鼠和两种植物的叶片为研究对象，研究人员发现了一种奇特的“生物光子”异常现象——这种异常现象会在生物死亡后停止，并获得了确凿的物理证据。这一发现意味着，所有活着的生命体——包括人类在内——或许真的会在生存状态下微弱地发光。

paragraphs.contentEn: At first glance, the findings might sound unbelievable but even more astonishing, in theory, visible wavelengths of light emitted by biological processes are said to be so faint that its easily outdone by the intense shine of ambient electromagnetic waves in the environment and radiant heat generated by our metabolism. That makes it a challenge to see light coming from living things.
paragraphs.contentZh: 刚看到这个研究发现时，你或许会觉得不可思议，但更令人称奇的是，从理论上来说，生物体在生命活动中所发出的可见光波极其微弱，很容易被周围环境中强烈的电磁波和人体新陈代谢所产生的辐射热所掩盖。这也是为什么我们很难观测到生物体自身发出的光。

paragraphs.contentEn: University of Calgary physicist Vahid Salari and his team claimed to have observed the glow – which is an ultraweak photon emission (UPE) produced by multiple living animals in strong contrast with their non-living bodies, as well as in a handful of plant leaves. The science behind biophotons stems from a heavily disputed topic. An array of biological processes distinctively generates bright displays of light in the form of chemiluminescence. Also, for years, the spontaneous sputtering of light waves anywhere from 200 to 1,000 nanometers in length were recorded from less noticeable reactions among a vast assortment of living cells, including cow heart tissue to bacterial colonies.
paragraphs.contentZh: 卡尔加里大学物理学家瓦希德・萨拉里及其研究团队表示，他们观察到了一种微弱的发光现象——即所谓的超微弱光子辐射（UPE），这种光由多种活体动物以及部分植物叶片释放，而这些生物死亡后则不会发出这种光。“生物光子”现象背后的科学基础源自一个长期存在争议的研究领域。科学家们已经知道，一系列特殊的生物过程能够以化学发光的形式产生亮光。此外，多年以来，研究人员还在大量不同类型的活细胞中（比如牛的心脏组织或细菌菌落），记录到一种不那么显眼的光波自发释放，波长范围在200至1000纳米之间。

paragraphs.contentEn: The source of this radiation could come from the effect of numerous reactive oxygen species that living cells produce when bothered by stresses such as heat, poisons, pathogens, or lack of nutrients. For example, if given enough molecules of hydrogen peroxide, materials like fats and proteins can undergo transformations that jumpstart their electrons into high gear and produce a suitably energetic photon or two as they settle back into place.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这种辐射可能源自活细胞在面对热量、毒素、病原体或营养缺乏等压力时所产生的大量活性氧（ROS）。比如，当细胞中存在足够多的过氧化氢分子时，脂肪和蛋白质等物质可能发生化学转化，使其内部电子跃迁至高能状态，随后，电子在回到稳定状态的过程中，便会释放出一两个能量足够的光子。

paragraphs.contentEn: Having the ability to remotely monitor the stress of individual tissues in whole human or animal patients, or even among crops or bacterial samples, could provide technicians and medical specialists with a powerful, non-invasive research or diagnostics tool. To determine whether the process could be scaled from isolated tissues to entire living subjects, the researchers used electron-multiplying charge-coupled device and charge-coupled device cameras to compare the faintest of light emissions from whole mice who were alive at first but later died.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如果能够远程监测人类或动物个体中某一组织的应激状态，甚至是农作物或细菌样本中的细胞反应，可能将为技术人员和医学专家提供一种强大的、非侵入性的研究或诊断工具。为了验证这一方法是否可以从单一组织扩展到完整的活体生物，研究人员使用电子倍增型电荷耦合器件（EMCCD）和普通电荷耦合器件（CCD）摄像机，对小鼠在存活状态及死亡之后所释放出的极其微弱的光进行了对比分析。

paragraphs.contentEn: There were four immobilized mice that were individually placed in a dark box and imaged for hour, before they were euthanized and imaged for another hour. They were warmed to body temperature even after death, to keep heat from being a variable. The researchers discovered that they could capture individual photons in the visible band of light emitting from the mouse cells prior and post death. The difference in the numbers of these photons were clear, with a significant drop in UPE in the measurement period after they were euthanized.
paragraphs.contentZh: 实验中，研究人员将四只小鼠分别固定，单独置于暗箱中持续成像一小时。随后对小鼠实施安乐死，并再次进行一小时成像。即使在小鼠死亡后，研究人员仍将其体温维持在正常水平，以排除温度变化带来的干扰。实验结果显示，研究人员成功捕捉到了小鼠细胞在死亡前后所释放的可见光波段的单个光子。对比后发现，光子数量差异十分明显，在小鼠被安乐死后的测量期间，其超微弱光子辐射（UPE）出现了显著下降。

paragraphs.contentEn: The same astonishing results took place after a process was done on thale cress (Arabidopsis thaliana) and dwarf umbrella tree (Heptapleurum arboricola) leaves. Stressing the plants with physical injuries and chemical agents provided substantial evidence that reactive oxygen species could in fact be behind the glow. “Our results show that the injury parts in all leaves were significantly brighter than the uninjured parts of the leaves during all 16 hours of imaging,” the researchers report. Scientific hopefuls are optimistic that the experiment fuels speculation that the faintest of godly glows produced by stressed cells might perhaps one day let us know if we’re in optimal health.
paragraphs.contentZh: 当研究人员以同样方式处理拟南芥（学名Arabidopsis thaliana）和鸭脚木（学名Heptapleurum arboricola）的叶片后，也观察到了同样令人惊讶的结果。通过施加物理损伤和化学刺激，实验为活性氧可能是发光机制核心因素的观点提供了有力证据。研究人员指出：“我们的实验结果显示，在长达16小时的成像过程中，所有叶片的受损区域始终明显亮于未受损区域。” 科学界的乐观者们期待，这项实验能进一步激发人们的猜想：这类细胞应激状态下产生的、极其微弱的“生命之光”，或许有朝一日能帮助我们判断自身是否处于最佳健康状态。
